spoken: Gubert and colleagues estimated severe food insecurity in Brazilian municipalities. Busker and colleagues forecast food crises in the Horn of Africa. Those studies predict different outcomes on different time scales. That makes it difficult to use their reported performance to choose a model for Cundinamarca.

spoken: Colombia's national statistics office, DANE, uses statistical models where survey samples are too small for reliable direct estimates. In its municipal bulletin for 2022, DANE flagged Gachetá's estimate for high uncertainty. That example shows why checking a local estimate's quality matters.

spoken: My objective is to establish criteria to guide the selection of predictive models of food insecurity at the municipal level. The aim is to give researchers a way to explain why a model deserves to be tested for a particular local use.

spoken: First, to identify predictive models used in studies of food insecurity at the municipal level. Second, to analyze model-selection criteria related to data characteristics, performance, and interpretability. Third, to integrate the identified criteria into a model-selection guide for the municipal context of Cundinamarca.

spoken: Foini and colleagues forecast insufficient food consumption. Their model beat the last observed value at longer horizons in Yemen and Syria. That simple baseline did better in the other four countries they studied. Model choice depends on evidence from the conditions where it will be used.

spoken: I place this study under the university's research line on Learning, Knowledge, Technologies, Communication and Digitalization. It fits that line because I examine how models turn data into evidence and what researchers should check before relying on the results.

spoken: At the center of the problem tree is the difficulty of justifying a model choice. Its roots are differences in study targets, data and evaluation, plus uncertainty about local fit. The main risk is choosing a model whose reported performance gives us little guidance for Cundinamarca.

spoken: The evidence I've reviewed points to a practical conclusion. The outcome and available data determine which tests are meaningful. The quality of those tests, together with explanations of the predictions, gives us a basis for judging whether a model fits its intended use.
